title: Heritage walk in Lucknow: imambaras, the Residency and old Awadh
seo_title: Heritage Walk in Lucknow: Historical Places, Routes, Museums
meta_description: Plan a heritage walk in Lucknow: Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza, Chhota Imambara, the Residency and Qaisarbagh, with routes, museums and tips for school groups.
summary: A heritage walk in Lucknow follows the capital of the Nawabs of Awadh from 1775 to 1856: the Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza and Chhota Imambara in Hussainabad, the Shah Najaf and Qaisarbagh by the Gomti, and the ruined Residency, besieged for nearly five months in 1857. Most stops cluster in two walkable areas.

paras: Lucknow is the best place in north India to see the architecture of an 18th and 19th century successor state. When Mughal power weakened, the governors of Awadh became independent rulers in practice. Asaf-ud-Daula moved the capital from Faizabad to Lucknow in 1775, and his successors filled the city with imambaras, mosques, gateways, palaces and gardens over the next eighty years.

It is also one of the main places to study 1857. The British Residency, where the East India Company's agent lived, was held under siege by Indian forces from June to November 1857, and its shell-scarred ruins have been kept as a memorial ever since. A walk here connects court culture, Shia religious architecture, colonial politics and the uprising in a single city.

Lucknow existed as a town under the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughals, and the Machhi Bhawan fort area near the river was its old centre. Little of that early fabric survives, because the Nawabs and later the British rebuilt it.

Asaf-ud-Daula built the Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza in 1784, partly as famine relief work. Saadat Ali Khan added palaces and a closer relationship with the Company. Ghazi-ud-din Haidar, who took the title of king in 1819, built the Shah Najaf Imambara; Muhammad Ali Shah built the Chhota Imambara (Hussainabad Imambara) in 1838; and Wajid Ali Shah built the Qaisarbagh palace complex around 1848 to 1850, before the Company annexed Awadh in 1856 and sent him to Calcutta.

After 1857 the British cleared large parts of the old city for roads and military lines. The [Mughal empire](mughal-empire.html) and [Indo-Islamic architecture](indo-islamic-architecture.html) guides give the background to the Nawabi style, which mixes Mughal forms with stucco, fish emblems and European details.

sections.h2: What you see on a Lucknow walk
paras: At the Bara Imambara, look up at the central hall, one of the largest vaulted halls of its time built without a supporting beam, and then climb into the Bhool Bhulaiya, the maze of passages in its upper storey. The building is made of brick and lime plaster rather than carved stone, which tells you about local materials and the speed of construction.

At the Residency, students trace the siege on the ground: the Baillie Guard Gate, the banqueting hall, the cemetery and the 1857 museum. A cemetery is a primary source in itself, which is the subject of the lecture [Cemeteries, epitaphs and public memory](cemeteries-epitaphs-and-public-memory.html). For comparison with the fighting in Delhi, see the [Kashmere Gate and 1857](kashmere-gate-1857.html) walk.

A Lucknow visit is arranged as a [study tour built for your group](a-study-tour-built-for-your-group.html), with the route, length and focus set around your class or team. A lecture before the visit helps: [Sacred architecture across communities](sacred-architecture-across-communities.html) suits the imambaras, and the [Oral history and neighbourhood memory lab](oral-history-and-neighbourhood-memory-lab.html) works well in the old city lanes of Chowk.

The Hussainabad group (Bara Imambara, Rumi Darwaza, Chhota Imambara, the clock tower and picture gallery) is walkable as one route. The Residency, Shah Najaf, Sikandar Bagh and Qaisarbagh form a second group about 3 km away; a short drive links the two. La Martiniere needs a vehicle. The imambaras are religious buildings, so dress modestly and check visiting rules, especially during Muharram.

stops.name: Bara Imambara
stops.note: Asaf-ud-Daula's imambara with its great vaulted hall, the Bhool Bhulaiya maze above and a stepwell (baoli) beside it.

stops.name: Asfi Mosque
stops.note: Mosque in the Bara Imambara complex on a high plinth with two minarets.

stops.name: Rumi Darwaza
stops.note: Monumental gateway west of the Bara Imambara, a symbol of the city.

stops.name: Chhota Imambara
stops.note: Muhammad Ali Shah's Hussainabad Imambara with chandeliers, Arabic calligraphy and a gilded dome.

stops.name: Hussainabad Clock Tower
stops.note: A tall Victorian-era clock tower beside the Hussainabad tank.

stops.name: Hussainabad Picture Gallery
stops.note: Baradari with portraits of the Nawabs of Awadh, opposite the unfinished Satkhanda tower.

stops.name: Chowk
stops.note: Old market of Lucknow, known for chikan embroidery, food streets and havelis.

stops.name: British Residency
stops.note: Ruined Residency compound with the Baillie Guard Gate, cemetery and 1857 memorial museum.

stops.name: Shah Najaf Imambara
stops.note: Ghazi-ud-din Haidar's tomb and imambara by the Gomti, with a white dome.

stops.name: Sikandar Bagh
stops.note: Walled garden where heavy fighting took place in November 1857.

stops.name: Qaisarbagh
stops.note: Surviving gateways and buildings of Wajid Ali Shah's palace complex, with the tomb of Saadat Ali Khan nearby.

stops.name: La Martiniere
stops.note: Claude Martin's palace Constantia, now a school, mixing European and Indian architectural ideas.

routes.name: 1857 and the Gomti
routes.length: About 3 hours, short rides between groups

museums.name: State Museum, Lucknow
museums.note: One of the larger museums in north India, with Mathura and Kushana sculpture, coins and Awadh material.

museums.name: 1857 Memorial Museum, Residency
museums.note: ASI museum on the siege, with a model of the Residency compound and period objects.

museums.name: Hussainabad Picture Gallery
museums.note: Portraits of the rulers of Awadh, useful for linking names to buildings.

best_time: October to March. Avoid the heat of May and June; check access to the imambaras around Muharram.

faq.q: Which historical places in Lucknow should a heritage walk include?
faq.a: The Bara Imambara with the Bhool Bhulaiya, Rumi Darwaza and Chhota Imambara in Hussainabad; then the Residency, Shah Najaf Imambara, Sikandar Bagh and Qaisarbagh near the Gomti. Add Chowk for the old market.

faq.q: Why is the Lucknow Residency important?
faq.a: It was the seat of the East India Company's agent at the Awadh court and was besieged by Indian forces from June to November 1857. The ruins were kept as they were, so the site shows the uprising on the ground.

faq.q: Is a Lucknow heritage walk good for schools?
faq.a: Yes. The Hussainabad monuments suit Class 7 and 8 history, and the Residency suits lessons on 1857. Walk the Hussainabad group in the morning and drive to the Residency group.
The State Museum has a strong sculpture and coin collection, the Residency has an 1857 museum, and the Hussainabad Picture Gallery shows the Nawabs of Awadh.

faq.q: Can a Lucknow heritage walk be arranged in Hindi?
faq.a: Yes. Talaash Heritage arranges Lucknow visits on request with an archaeologist or historian, in English or Hindi, for schools, colleges, companies and private groups.

posts.hook: The Bara Imambara was a famine relief project.
posts.caption: Asaf-ud-Daula began it in 1784, a famine year, and the building gave paid work to thousands. Its vaulted hall is built in brick and lime, with no beams holding up the roof.

posts.hook: At the Residency, read the walls.
posts.caption: Shell and bullet marks from 1857 are still on the buildings. Walk from the Baillie Guard Gate to the cemetery and you can trace the five-month siege on the ground.
